'''''Fuchsia paniculata'''''  is a plant of the genus ''[[Fuchsia]]'' native to Central America. It belongs to the section Schufia and is most closely related to ''[[Fuchsia arborescens]]''.<ref name="Berry2004">{{cite journal |author=Berry, Paul E. |author2=William J. Hahn |author3=Kenneth J. Sytsma |author4=Jocelyn C. Hall |author5=Austin Mast |date=2004|title=Phylogenetic relationships and biogeography of ''Fuchsia'' (Onagraceae) based on noncoding nuclear and chloroplast DNA data|journal=American Journal of Botany|volume=91|issue=4|pages=601–14|doi=10.3732/ajb.91.4.601|pmid=21653416}}</ref>
==Description==
''Fuchsia paniculata'' is a tall shrub or small tree, typically reaching {{convert|3-8|m|ft}} in height. It usually has smooth, erect branches.

The fruit is nearly round, 4-9 mm long and 4-7 mm thick, with a bluish-purple color and a whitish, waxy coating. The seeds are 1-1.4 mm long and 0.5-0.8 mm thick.<ref name="Species Page/ Botany, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution u585">{{cite web | title=Onagraceae | website=Species Page/ Botany, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution | url=https://naturalhistory2.si.edu/botany/onagraceae/speciesdescr.cfm?myID=3679 | access-date=2024-04-16}}</ref>
